variables.name: REMOTE_BUILD_QUEUE
variables.values: Name of an LSF queue (LSF is the batch scheduler). The text is passed unchanged to bsub -q. The script does not check it.
variables.default: sw-build when the variable is unset or empty.
variables.effect: Selects the LSF queue that receives the build job (bsub -q on bin/bsub-build:74).
variables.notes: bin/bsub-build is run by the make build targets when remote mode is on (GNUmakefile:399, outside this area). README.md:511 documents the variable.

variables.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES

readers.mechanism: the value is checked by require_positive_int (bin/bsub-build:19)

variables.values: Positive decimal integer (number of cores). The script rejects text that holds any character other than 0-9, and the exact text 0. It then prints 'bsub-build: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES must be a positive integer' and exits with code 2.
variables.default: 16 when the variable is unset or empty.
variables.effect: Sets the number of cores that the LSF job reserves (rusage cores=, bin/bsub-build:75). The same number is exported inside the job as NPROC_BUILD and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS (bin/bsub-build:53). It also sets the default memory reservation: cores x 8192 MB (bin/bsub-build:32).
variables.notes: Unit: cores. A value with a leading zero passes the check. When REMOTE_BUILD_MEM is not set, bash arithmetic on line 32 then reads the value as octal: 010 gives 8 x 8192 MB, and 08 stops the script with a bash error (checked with bash 5.1.16). GNUmakefile:399 sets REMOTE_BUILD_CORES=<N> for the script when make was given -jN (outside this area). README.md:512 documents the variable.

variables.name: REMOTE_BUILD_MEM
variables.values: A number of megabytes. The script does not check the text. It is passed to bsub inside -R "rusage[mem=<value>,cores=<cores>]" (bin/bsub-build:75).
variables.default: cores x 8192 when the variable is unset or empty. With the default 16 cores this is 131072 (MB).
variables.effect: Sets the memory that the LSF build job reserves.
variables.notes: The script prints the value with the suffix M in its log line (bin/bsub-build:73). README.md:513 gives the unit as MB. A comment on bin/bsub-build:18 says that bsub itself rejects a bad value.

variables.name: ENABLE_FUSE_STATS

readers.mechanism: shell indirect expansion ${!var}; var takes each name of the fixed list on bin/bsub-build:54

setters.value: the value of the submitting shell, quoted with printf %q
setters.why: exports the same build input inside the LSF job, because the job starts from an empty environment (env -i, bin/bsub-build:65)

variables.values: bin/bsub-build forwards any non-empty text unchanged. It does not parse the text.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the variable is not forwarded. The make on the worker then uses its own default (ENABLE_FUSE_STATS ?= ON, GNUmakefile:268, outside this area).
variables.effect: When the variable is non-empty in the submitting shell, the remote build job gets the same value.
variables.notes: The value itself is used by the GNUmakefile, which passes it to CMake as -DENABLE_FUSE_STATS (for example GNUmakefile:580). That file is outside this area.

variables.name: CCACHE_DISABLE

readers.mechanism: shell indirect expansion ${!var}; var takes each name of the fixed list on bin/bsub-build:54

setters.value: the value of the submitting shell, quoted with printf %q
setters.why: exports the same setting inside the LSF job, because the job starts from an empty environment (env -i, bin/bsub-build:65)
turns ccache (the compiler cache) off before the second, timed make, so that the timed rebuild really compiles

variables.values: bin/bsub-build forwards any non-empty text unchanged. The variable belongs to ccache. No script in this area parses it.
variables.default: Unset or empty: bin/bsub-build does not forward it. bin/time_rebuild always exports it as 1 after its first make.
variables.effect: bin/bsub-build: the remote build job gets the same value as the submitting shell. bin/time_rebuild: the timed make runs with ccache off.
variables.notes: bin/time_rebuild runs make, exports the variable, touches h/tron/attributes.hpp, then runs time make (bin/time_rebuild:17-20).

variables.name: XDG_CACHE_HOME

readers.mechanism: shell indirect expansion ${!var}; var takes each name of the fixed list on bin/bsub-build:54

setters.value: the value of the submitting shell, quoted with printf %q
setters.why: exports the same cache location inside the LSF job, because the job starts from an empty environment (env -i, bin/bsub-build:65)

variables.values: Path to a directory. bin/bsub-build forwards any non-empty text unchanged.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the variable is not forwarded.
variables.effect: When the variable is non-empty in the submitting shell, the remote build job gets the same value.
variables.notes: The script comment (bin/bsub-build:51-52) gives the purpose: the Nix cache location travels with the job when the submitter set it.

variables.name: HOME

setters.value: the HOME of the submitting shell
setters.why: the remote job runs under env -i, and the script passes HOME explicitly
the self-test (--self-test) calls the script functions with a fake home directory

variables.values: Path to the home directory of the user.
variables.default: bin/bsub-build: unset stops the script with the bash error 'HOME: unbound variable' (set -u, bin/bsub-build:12). bin/scratch-dir.sh: unset or empty is replaced by /nonexistent. The cd then fails and the script makes no scratch mapping, so the build directory is a plain directory.
variables.effect: bin/bsub-build passes the value as HOME of the remote job. bin/scratch-dir.sh moves a build directory to scratch storage only when the physical path of HOME lies under TRON_HOME_ROOT and the checkout lies under HOME (bin/scratch-dir.sh:24). The path of the checkout relative to HOME becomes part of the scratch path (bin/scratch-dir.sh:25).
variables.notes: See TRON_HOME_ROOT and TRON_SCRATCH_USERS for the full scratch path.

variables.name: USER

setters.value: the USER of the submitting shell, or the output of id -un
setters.why: the remote job runs under env -i, and the script passes USER explicitly

variables.values: A user name. The text is not checked.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the script uses the output of id -un.
variables.effect: Becomes USER of the remote build job.

variables.name: TERM

setters.value: the TERM of the submitting shell, or dumb
setters.why: the remote job runs under env -i, and the script passes TERM explicitly

variables.values: A terminal type name. The text is not checked.
variables.default: Unset or empty: dumb.
variables.effect: Becomes TERM of the remote build job.

variables.name: LANG

setters.value: the LANG of the submitting shell, or C.UTF-8
setters.why: the remote job runs under env -i, and the script passes LANG explicitly

variables.values: A locale name. The text is not checked.
variables.default: Unset or empty: C.UTF-8.
variables.effect: Becomes LANG of the remote build job.
variables.notes: The script comment (bin/bsub-build:63-64) says LANG must stay UTF-8: CMake archive extraction fails on non-ASCII paths under the C locale. A non-UTF-8 LANG in the submitting shell is still forwarded unchanged.

variables.name: REMOTE

setters.why: the job runs make again on the worker, and REMOTE=0 stops that make from submitting itself again (comment on bin/bsub-build:47)

variables.values: No script in this area reads it. The reader is the GNUmakefile, which accepts exactly one of 0, 1, sku0, sku1 and stops with an error on other text (GNUmakefile:143-160, outside this area).
variables.default: bin/bsub-build always exports 0 inside the job. For the default of the reader see GNUmakefile:130-137 (outside this area).
variables.effect: Inside the LSF job, make builds on the worker itself.
variables.notes: bin/bsub-build does not read REMOTE. Its error text 'REMOTE is set but bsub is not on PATH' (bin/bsub-build:37) is only a message. The comment on bin/bsub-build:48 also names TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION, but the script neither reads nor sets that name.

variables.name: NPROC_BUILD

setters.why: keeps the job count of the build on the worker at the number of reserved cores (comment on bin/bsub-build:48-51)

variables.values: No script in this area reads it. bin/bsub-build sets a positive integer.
variables.default: bin/bsub-build always exports it inside the job. The reader computes its own default when the variable is not defined (GNUmakefile:95-97, outside this area).
variables.effect: The make on the worker uses it as the parallel job count (cmake --build -j $(NPROC_BUILD), for example GNUmakefile:404, outside this area).
variables.notes: The LSF reservation schedules the worker but does not confine the job to the reserved cores (comment on bin/bsub-build:50-51).

variables.name: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS

setters.why: keeps the cargo job count on the worker at the number of reserved cores (comment on bin/bsub-build:48-51)

variables.values: No TRON code reads it: bin/bsub-build:49 and bin/bsub-build:53 are the only mentions in the checkout. cargo (the Rust build tool) reads it.
variables.default: bin/bsub-build always exports it inside the job.
variables.effect: Limits the number of parallel cargo jobs in the remote build.

variables.name: TRON_FEATURE_BRANCH_BUILD
variables.values: Any non-empty value enables it. The text is not parsed, so 0 or false also enable it.
variables.default: Unset or empty: off. The version is then the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, the git describe text on a release-* branch, or <date as YYYY.MM.DD>-<8-character commit hash>, with -<branch> added on a named branch other than main (bin/get-version.sh:14, 30-44).
variables.effect: On a named branch other than main and release-*, the version becomes <tag>+feature.<branch>.<commits since tag>.g<8-character commit hash>. The tag is the nearest reachable tag that matches v[0-9]*. If that tag does not have the form v<number>[.<number>...] with an optional -devN, -tcN or -rcN, the script prints an error and exits with code 1.
variables.notes: The variable has no effect on main, on release-* branches and on a detached HEAD (bin/get-version.sh:17-18). When it is on, an exact tag on HEAD is not used alone (bin/get-version.sh:30). Characters of the branch name outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot and minus become dots (bin/get-version.sh:10). The suffix -dirty is still added for a modified tree (bin/get-version.sh:47-49). bin/get-version.sh is called by bin/make-version.sh:13 (version text compiled into the binaries) and by bin/get-deb-version.sh:14 (Debian package version, which GNUmakefile:365 computes on every make run). Setters outside this area: .github/workflows/publish-deb.yml:90, bin/ci/test-get-deb-version.sh. Documented in README.ci.md:362 and packaging/tron-host/README:204.

variables.name: TRON_SCRATCH_USERS
variables.values: Path to a directory: the root of the per-user scratch trees.
variables.default: /scratch/users when the variable is unset or empty.
variables.effect: Sets the root under which build directories (gen, gen-deb, gen-deb-host, gen-tsan, gen-asan, gen-coverage) are created. The checkout gets a symbolic link to <root>/<HOME relative to TRON_HOME_ROOT>/tmp/<checkout path relative to HOME>/<directory> (bin/scratch-dir.sh:25).
variables.notes: The value is also used to recognise links that point into a scratch tree (bin/scratch-dir.sh:51, bin/scratch-dir.sh:122). The script makes no scratch link when CI is non-empty, when cmake is older than 3.24, when the checkout is not under HOME, or when the target cannot be created. The GNUmakefile runs the script when make starts (GNUmakefile:274) and from the build-directory targets (GNUmakefile:579, 636, 691, 728, 752), all outside this area. bin/scratch-dir.sh:11 is the only mention of the name in the checkout, so no document describes it.

variables.name: TRON_HOME_ROOT
variables.values: Path to a directory: the parent directory of the home directories.
variables.default: /home when the variable is unset or empty.
variables.effect: A build directory moves to scratch storage only when the physical path of HOME lies below this directory (bin/scratch-dir.sh:24). The part of HOME after this prefix names the per-user folder under TRON_SCRATCH_USERS (bin/scratch-dir.sh:25).
variables.notes: bin/scratch-dir.sh:12 is the only mention of the name in the checkout, so no document describes it. The self-test does not set this variable. It overrides the internal shell variable HOME_ROOT instead (bin/scratch-dir.sh:209).

variables.name: CI

setters.why: self-test case: a CI job gets a plain directory even under /home
self-test case: a CI job replaces a retained scratch link by a plain directory

variables.values: Any non-empty value enables it. The text is not parsed.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the normal scratch-link logic runs.
variables.effect: When CI is non-empty the script never uses scratch storage. It removes an existing symbolic link for the build directory and creates a plain directory (bin/scratch-dir.sh:108-112).
variables.notes: The self-test removes CI from its own environment first (unset CI, bin/scratch-dir.sh:191), so an inherited CI value does not change the other self-test cases. The reason is in the comment on bin/scratch-dir.sh:104-107: each CI job must start from a clean tree.

variables.name: PATH

setters.why: puts the stub cmake of the self-test first, so the result does not depend on the installed CMake (comment on bin/scratch-dir.sh:196)

variables.values: Colon-separated list of directories, as usual for PATH.
variables.default: The script has no default of its own. bash supplies its built-in PATH when the caller gives none (checked with bash 5.1.16), and the script prepends its directory to that value.
variables.effect: Only the self-test (bin/scratch-dir.sh --self-test) reads the text of PATH. It prepends the directory that holds the stub cmake for each tested call.
variables.notes: The other scripts of this area use PATH only through command lookup, for example command -v bsub on bin/bsub-build:36. Those lookups are not listed as reads.

variables.name: STUB_CMAKE_VERSION

readers.program: stub cmake script that bin/scratch-dir.sh --self-test writes to <temporary directory>/bin/cmake

setters.why: the stub reports a CMake older than 3.24, so the self-test covers the plain-directory case
same, for the case of a directory that CMake already configured
same, for the case of a directory that holds a build lock

variables.values: A CMake version text, for example 3.22.1. The stub prints 'cmake version <value>'.
variables.default: 3.24.0 when the variable is unset or empty.
variables.effect: Sets the version that the stub cmake reports during the self-test. cmake_follows_links (bin/scratch-dir.sh:77) compares the reported version with 3.24. A lower version makes scratch_dir keep a plain directory.
variables.notes: The variable exists only for the self-test. The self-test calls without an explicit value inherit the variable from the caller, so an exported STUB_CMAKE_VERSION changes those cases. flake.nix:2211 runs the self-test (outside this area).

variables.name: TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT

setters.why: strategy blast of the load experiment
strategy chunk of the load experiment
strategy queueing of the load experiment

variables.values: No script in this area reads it. The reader is product code outside this area: h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1836 parses the text with std::atoi.
variables.default: bin/analyze-tps always sets it. In the reader, an unset variable means 100000000 (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1838).
variables.effect: bin/analyze-tps places the assignment before gen/runtron in the command that ssh runs on the remote host (bin/analyze-tps:70). The reader uses the number as the live token limit of the scheduler. When the model configuration has max_minibatches above 0, the limit is capped at max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1839-1842).
variables.notes: The assignment applies to gen/runtron only, not to the make gen/runtron step before it. The string is built in the shell variable env_vars.

variables.name: TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT

setters.why: strategy blast of the load experiment
strategy chunk of the load experiment
strategy queueing of the load experiment

variables.values: No script in this area reads it. The reader is product code outside this area: h/libtron.hpp:199 parses the text with std::stoul.
variables.default: bin/analyze-tps always sets it. In the reader, an unset variable means 128 (h/libtron.hpp:202).
variables.effect: bin/analyze-tps places the assignment before gen/runtron in the command that ssh runs on the remote host (bin/analyze-tps:70). The reader uses the number as the prompt chunk size: how many prompt tokens are processed at once (comment on h/libtron.hpp:193-195).
variables.notes: The reader stores the value in a function-local static on the first call of get_prompt_chunk_size (h/libtron.hpp:198). The assignment applies to gen/runtron only, not to the make gen/runtron step before it.

variables.name: OSTYPE

readers.mechanism: shell $NAME; bash sets the variable at startup unless it inherits one
shell $NAME; bash sets the variable at startup unless it inherits one
shell $NAME; bash sets the variable at startup unless it inherits one
shell $NAME; bash sets the variable at startup unless it inherits one

variables.values: Text compared with the pattern darwin*. Any value that starts with darwin selects the macOS code path.
variables.default: When the caller does not export it, bash fills it with its own OS type (linux-gnu on this Linux host). The scripts then use the Linux code path.
variables.effect: With a darwin* value, bin/remove_whitespace.sh reads the file mode with stat -f '%Lp' and calls chmod -- MODE PATH, and bin/update-generated-file.sh copies only the mode of the old file. Otherwise the scripts use stat -c '%a', chmod MODE -- PATH and cp --attributes-only --preserve=mode,ownership,xattr.
variables.notes: An exported value wins over the value bash would set: OSTYPE=darwin22 stayed in effect in a test with bash 5.1.16. Two CI tests use this to force the macOS path on Linux: bin/ci/test-remove-whitespace.sh:83 and bin/ci/test-generated-output-staging.sh:564 (outside this area). bin/update-generated-file.sh is run by CMake build steps (for example src/CMakeLists.txt:20). bin/remove_whitespace.sh is the whitespace formatter (GNUmakefile:973).

variables.name: pci_id

readers.mechanism: shell $NAME; the script never assigns the name
shell $NAME; the script never assigns the name

variables.values: Expected form vvvv:dddd: 4 hex digits, a colon, 4 hex digits (PCI vendor ID and device ID). The value is passed unquoted as the second argument of bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh.
variables.default: Unset or empty: bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh receives only the card address. It prints the warning 'You did not specify a Vendor:Device (vvvv:dddd), unable to validate' and binds the card anyway (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:129).
variables.effect: In bind mode (first argument not equal to unbind), bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh checks that this vendor and device ID is present at each card address before it binds the card to the vfio-pci driver (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:121-127).
variables.notes: The name is lower case. No comment or document in the checkout describes this read. The card list itself comes from the fixed filter lspci -d 8200: (bin/bind-cards.sh:7), so the variable does not select cards. Text that matches none of the three patterns of bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh makes that script exit with code 1 (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:83-85), and bin/bind-cards.sh then stops (set -e). Text of the form dddd:bb:dd.f or bb:dd.f replaces the card address (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:78-82). bin/reload_cards.sh:5 and bin/reset-cards:2 assign pci_id themselves, so they do not read the environment.

variables.name: SUDO_UID

readers.mechanism: shell $NAME; the script never assigns the name

variables.values: A numeric user ID. sudo sets it to the ID of the user who called sudo.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the command becomes chown :positron <path>, which changes only the group.
variables.effect: After the bind, the script makes this user the owner of /dev/vfio/<IOMMU group number> and sets the group to positron. It then sets mode 660 (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:183).
variables.notes: The header comment (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:55-56) names $SUDO_USER, but the code reads SUDO_UID. The script must run as root (EUID check on bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:64). EUID is a bash internal variable and is not taken from the environment. bin/bind-cards.sh:27 and bin/reload_cards.sh:36 call this script.

variables.name: start_address

readers.mechanism: shell $NAME read before the first assignment; the first loop pass takes the inherited value

variables.values: Hexadecimal digits without the 0x prefix. The script puts 0x in front and uses the text in bash arithmetic.
variables.default: Unset or empty: the value counts as 0 (checked with bash 5.1.16), so the first address is the base address 0x37000000000.
variables.effect: On the first pass of the loop, the inherited value is added to the base address 0x37000000000. The result is the address that ./iotools mmio_write64 writes and ./iotools mmio_read64 reads. On each later pass the address of the previous pass is added to the base address again.
variables.notes: The script reads a range column from address_map_1.csv (bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh:13) but never uses it. The sibling script assigns start_address from that column first (bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_2.sh:21) and does not read the environment. No comment or document in the checkout describes this read. The script writes to device memory, so an exported start_address changes which addresses are written.

variables.name: CROSS_COMPILE

readers.mechanism: Make $(NAME); the makefile never assigns the name

variables.values: Text placed directly before gcc to form the compiler command, for example the prefix of a cross toolchain.
variables.default: Unset: the compiler command is gcc.
variables.effect: Sets CC to <value>gcc for compiling and linking iotools.
variables.notes: The makefile assigns CC itself (bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:20), so a CC environment variable has no effect unless make runs with -e. Described in bin/iotools-1.5/README. bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: DEBUG
variables.values: Exactly 0 (blanks are stripped) selects the optimised build. Any other value selects the debug build. An empty value also selects the debug build.
variables.default: 1 when unset: debug build with -O0 -ggdb.
variables.effect: 0 compiles iotools with -O2 -DNDEBUG. Any other value compiles with -O0 -ggdb.
variables.notes: The top-level GNUmakefile tests a variable of the same name for another purpose (ifdef DEBUG, GNUmakefile:369, outside this area). bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: STATIC
variables.values: Exactly 0 (blanks are stripped) turns static linking off. Any other value turns it on. An empty value also turns it on.
variables.default: 1 when unset: the flag -static is added.
variables.effect: Any value other than 0 adds -static to CFLAGS, which the compile and link commands use. With 0 the makefile does not assign IOTOOLS_STATIC.
variables.notes: See IOTOOLS_STATIC for what happens with STATIC=0. bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: IOTOOLS_STATIC

readers.mechanism: Make $(NAME); the makefile assigns the name only when STATIC is not 0 (bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:26-28)

variables.values: Compiler flag text. It is used unchanged inside CFLAGS.
variables.default: With STATIC not equal to 0 (the default) the makefile sets it to -static and an environment value is ignored. With STATIC=0 and no environment value it is empty.
variables.effect: Only with STATIC=0: an IOTOOLS_STATIC value from the environment is added to CFLAGS.
variables.notes: This is a side effect of the conditional assignment, not a documented option: bin/iotools-1.5/README does not name it. Checked with GNU Make 4.3 on a copy of the same construct. bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: ARCHFLAGS

readers.mechanism: Make $(NAME); the makefile never assigns the name

variables.values: Compiler flag text. It is used unchanged inside CFLAGS.
variables.default: Unset: empty, no extra flags.
variables.effect: Adds the given flags to CFLAGS, which the compile and link commands of iotools use.
variables.notes: bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: EXTRA_CFLAGS

readers.mechanism: Make $(NAME); the makefile never assigns the name

variables.values: Compiler flag text. It is used unchanged inside CFLAGS.

variables.notes: CFLAGS also holds -Wall -Werror (bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:36). bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: LDFLAGS

variables.values: Linker flag text. It is used unchanged in the link command.

variables.effect: Adds the given flags to the command that links the iotools binary.
variables.notes: bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: SBINDIR
variables.values: Path to a directory.
variables.default: /usr/local/sbin when unset. An empty value from the environment stays empty.
variables.effect: Target install copies the iotools binary into this directory and runs <directory>/iotools --make-links. Target rinstall uses the same path on the remote host.
variables.notes: bin/iotools-1.5 is a vendored copy of Google iotools 1.5. No TRON build file runs this makefile: the only mentions of the directory outside it are lint exclusions (GNUmakefile:959, flake.nix:2040, flake.nix:2085, flake.nix:2418). A person must run make inside bin/iotools-1.5 by hand.

variables.name: RUSER
variables.values: A user name on the remote host.
variables.default: root when unset.

wrappers.description: Self-test helper of bin/scratch-dir.sh. It calls one script function (scratch_dir or remove_dir) with PATH and HOME set for that call, and with the internal shell variables HOME_ROOT and SCRATCH_USERS overridden (bin/scratch-dir.sh:209-210). Callers add STUB_CMAKE_VERSION=3.22.1 or CI=true in front of the call. It does not read a variable by a name that the caller passes.
Validation helper, not an environment reader. Callers pass a value and the variable name for the error text. The only call is for REMOTE_BUILD_CORES (bin/bsub-build:27).

dynamic_sites.description: The name is taken from the loop variable var and read with indirect expansion ${!var}. Line 56 exports the same name inside the LSF job. Possible names: the fixed list on bin/bsub-build:54, which is ENABLE_FUSE_STATS, CCACHE_DISABLE, XDG_CACHE_HOME.

The remote command starts with env -i, so the LSF job does not inherit the environment of the submitting shell. The job sees only HOME, USER, TERM and LANG from this line, the exports of the payload (REMOTE, NPROC_BUILD, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS and the forwarded names of line 54), and what the login shell (bash -lc) and nix develop add on the worker.

The assignments are held in the shell variable env_vars and pasted into the command that ssh runs on the remote host, directly before gen/runtron. Possible names: TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT and TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT (bin/analyze-tps:53, 56, 59).

The script sources /tools/intelFPGA_pro/23.4/environment.sh, a file outside the checkout (Intel Quartus tools). The variables that this file sets are not known from the checkout. They apply to the later commands of the script, for example bin/load_fpga (bin/reload_cards.sh:30).
The command env with no arguments prints every environment variable of the script to standard output. No single name is read.
The self-test writes a stub cmake script to a temporary directory. The emitted /bin/sh script reads STUB_CMAKE_VERSION with a default of 3.24.0.

notes: All 26 files of the area were read in full. None was skipped. Files with a named environment read or set: bin/analyze-tps, bin/bind-cards.sh, bin/bsub-build, bin/get-version.sh, bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile, bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh, bin/remove_whitespace.sh, bin/scratch-dir.sh, bin/time_rebuild, bin/update-generated-file.sh, bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh. bin/reload_cards.sh has no named read; see dynamic_sites. Files that use only positional arguments and their own variables (no environment read or set): bin/generate_plugins_header.sh, bin/get-card-state, bin/get-deb-version.sh, bin/ingest-cabal, bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_2.sh, bin/list-tests, bin/make-version.sh, bin/metadata_builder, bin/patch_pci_ids.sh, bin/repeat, bin/replace_symlinks.sh, bin/reset-cards, bin/run-if-outputs-missing.sh, bin/write-generated-state.sh. bin/get-deb-version.sh:14 and bin/make-version.sh:13 call bin/get-version.sh, so they pass TRON_FEATURE_BRANCH_BUILD on without naming it. Not listed, on purpose: (1) bash internal variables: RANDOM (bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh:23, bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_2.sh:27), SECONDS (bin/repeat:42, 45; only differences are used, so an inherited start value changes nothing), EUID (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:64; bash ignores an inherited value), BASH_SOURCE and BASH_REMATCH (bin/get-deb-version.sh). (2) HOME_ROOT and SCRATCH_USERS on bin/scratch-dir.sh:209-210: these are internal shell variables of the script, assigned on lines 11-12 and overridden for one function call in the self-test; no program reads them from the environment. (3) Names that appear only in comments: TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION (bin/bsub-build:48), SUDO_USER (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:56), NIX_* (bin/bsub-build:62). (4) The shell variable remote of bin/analyze-tps is used inside a function on line 68 but assigned from the first argument on line 85 before the function is called. Implicit reads by tools that the scripts start are not in the script text and are not listed. Two that a reader may meet: mktemp -d with no template on bin/scratch-dir.sh:190 uses TMPDIR (behaviour of coreutils mktemp, not stated in the checkout), and the built-in %.o rule of GNU make, which compiles the iotools objects, also expands CPPFLAGS and TARGET_ARCH (behaviour of GNU make, not stated in the checkout). Two reads look unintended and may be script defects: pci_id in bin/bind-cards.sh and start_address in bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh. They are listed because the caller's environment does supply the value. Sites outside this area are named only in notes text, never in readers or setters. Shell and make semantics that the entries rely on were checked on this host with bash 5.1.16 and GNU Make 4.3, using stand-alone one-line tests, not repository scripts: an inherited OSTYPE is kept; an empty hex operand 0x counts as 0; ${NAME:-default} also replaces an empty value; an environment value overrides the built-in RM; an environment CC does not override the makefile assignment; ?= keeps an empty environment value.
